newsitem.title: GERMANY: N.Europe rapeseed sellers resist price pressure.
newsitem.headline: N.Europe rapeseed sellers resist price pressure.

text.p: Northern Europe rapeseed sellers are resisting pressure from buyers for lower prices following a decline in world oilseeds markets on bearish U.S. soybean data, brokers said on Friday.
"Sellers cite the lower harvest in Europe and elsewhere, which means rapeseed will be tight in the 1996/97 season," one broker said.
East Europe would become a net importer of rapeseed and Scandinavia would also depend on northwest European supply.
The firm dollar versus European currencies also absorbed some of the downward pressure on prices.
But Eastern European sunseed was offsetting some of the tightness in rape.
Buyers free Hamburg offered 465 marks a tonne for nearby rapeseed, 7.50 marks less than last week.
Buyers at German delivery points other than Hamburg pegged October at 437.50-457.50 marks, down from 447-470 last week.
November ciffo seed in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp range dropped to 457.50 marks from 480 previously.
Rape oil prices took further support from the prospect of possible disruption from consumer opposition to genetically modified U.S. soybeans.
Environmental and consumer groups this week renewed their protests against the new products.
Nov-Jan rape oil cif Rotterdam remained at an untypical $4.00 premium over soyoil at $94.00/100 kg today, but the premium at some stages has been $5.
The November position on the Paris Matif futures exchange was last in a 456-459 marks bid/offer range compared with Thursday's 456 close and values of around 463 a week ago.
Local rape meal sellers (34 percent protein) were 0.25-0.50 mark higher than last week at 30.50-30.75 marks/100 kg (Oct) while Nov/Jan meal was down 0.25 at 29.75.
Nov/Jan rape oil was at 83.75 marks/100 kg, down 1.75, and Feb/April oil was newly quoted at 86.00.
